newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN investigator reports Taleban attacks on women.
newsitem.headline: UN investigator reports Taleban attacks on women.

text.p: The United Nations special investigator on violence against women expressed concern on Friday over reports of the Islamic Taleban movement abusing and even attacking Afghan girls and women.

Radhika Coomaraswamy, a Sri Lankan lawyer, urgently appealed to Mullah Mohammad Omar, leader of the Supreme Council of the Taleban movement, to "reinstate respect for human rights of women" by lifting its ban on women's participation in society.

The Taleban, who seized Kabul on September 27, demand that their strict version of Islamic Sharia law be imposed throughout the country. The U.N. Security Council has denounced what it called discrimination against girls and women, who have been forbidden to work or attend schools and universities.

Coomaraswamy, in a statement issued through the U.N. European headquarters in Geneva, expressed her "earnest concern over persisting reports of violence perpetrated by the Taleban movement against Afghan women and girls".

"Since the capture of Kabul by the Taleban movement over one month ago, an instituted policy of banning women from the workplace, ordering women to stay at home and denying girls access to schools has been implemented.
"The special rapporteur is receiving continuing reports that women are being attacked in the streets and severely beaten," she added.

Coomaraswamy reports to the 53-member U.N. Human Rights Commission, which opens its next annual meeting in March. She reminded the Taleban leadership of Afghanistan's obligations under the international human rights treaties it has ratified.
These included rights to: liberty and security of persons, to equal status and to be free from all forms of discrimination, to equal access to education and to work.

"The special rapporteur urgently appeals to the leader of Supreme Council of the Taleban movement, Mullah Mohammad Omar, to reinstate respect for human rights of women by lifting its ban on women's participation in civil society...," she said.
